name: Communication Sciences & Disorders
summary: Communication Sciences and Disorders studies how people speak, hear, and understand language and what happens when these abilities are impaired. It is the pathway to careers in speech-language pathology and audiology.
description: Communication Sciences and Disorders majors study anatomy and physiology of speech and hearing, phonetics, speech science, hearing science, language development, neurological bases of communication, and disorders of speech, language, voice, fluency, swallowing, and hearing. They observe clinical sessions and learn assessment and treatment basics. A master's degree is required to become a licensed speech-language pathologist and a doctorate (AuD) to become an audiologist, so most graduates continue to graduate school. With a bachelor's degree, graduates can work as speech-language pathology assistants.
